text: Confirmed: both balancers index into an empty target slice in `Next`, so they panic instead of returning nil. I'm fixing `middleware/proxy.go` so `randomBalancer.Next` and `roundRobinBalancer.Next` return nil when there are no targets, and verifying with the full test suite. ETA ~8 min.

Fixed. Both balancers in `middleware/proxy.go` now return nil when there are no targets instead of panicking:

- `randomBalancer.Next`: added `if len(b.targets) == 0 { return nil }` inside the existing read-lock, before `b.random.Intn(len(b.targets))`.
- `roundRobinBalancer.Next`: added `if len(b.targets) == 0 { return nil }` before the `% uint32(len(b.targets))` modulo.

So `NewRandomBalancer(nil).Next(c)` and `NewRoundRobinBalancer([]*ProxyTarget{}).Next(c)` both return nil and your handler can respond with a "no target available" error. Verified: with targets present behavior is unchanged (single target returned, round-robin still alternates A,B,A,B), `go vet` is clean, and the full suite (`go test ./...`) passes with no pre-existing test broken. Only `middleware/proxy.go` was modified.

Understood: `c.Path()` should be "" when no route matched (it's documented as the path of the matched route). I'm tracing where the router sets the context path for unmatched requests and fixing it so the not-found case reports an empty path, while matched routes (and the 404 handling itself) stay unchanged. ETA ~10 min.

Right: `Scheme()` currently returns whatever the header contains, even when it isn't a real scheme. I'm changing it so only valid schemes (http/https) are accepted from the headers, falling through to the next source (X-Forwarded-Protocol, X-Forwarded-Ssl, X-Url-Scheme) and finally to "http". ETA ~10 min.

Fixed. The cause was in `router.go`: `Router.Find` started by storing the *requested* URL path into the context (`ctx.path = path`) before routing, so an unmatched request kept that value. For matched routes the path is (re)set to the registered route pattern at the end of `Find`, which is why only unmatched requests were wrong.

I removed that premature assignment, so now:
- unmatched request → `c.Path()` is `""` inside `HTTPErrorHandler` (status still 404, handler still called),
- matched route → `c.Path()` is still the route pattern (e.g. `/users/:id`),
- the 405/method-not-allowed case still reports the matched route pattern,
- static/group route handling is unaffected.

Verified with throwaway tests (deleted afterwards) and the full suite (`go test -count=1 ./...`) passes exactly as before, `go vet` clean.

Confirmed: the map branch of the binder (`bindData` in `bind.go`) always assigns `v[0]` — a single string — regardless of the map's element type, which panics for `map[string][]string` and loses values for `map[string]interface{}`. I'm fixing it so repeated keys keep all their values (`?tag=a&tag=b` → `{"tag": ["a","b"]}`), while `map[string]string` and all struct binding stay as before. ETA ~10 min.

Fixed in `bind.go` (the map branch of `DefaultBinder.bindData`). It always assigned `v[0]` — a single string — regardless of the map's element type, hence the panic for `map[string][]string` and the lost values for `map[string]interface{}`.

Now:
- `map[string][]string` → all values are kept: `?tag=a&tag=b` gives `{"tag": ["a","b"]}` (no panic); `?tag=a` gives `{"tag": ["a"]}`. Non-string element types (e.g. `map[string][]int`) are parsed with the existing helper instead of panicking.
- `map[string]interface{}` → a key with several values now holds the `[]string` of all values; a key with a single value still holds a plain string (unchanged from before).
- `map[string]string` and all struct/body binding are unchanged.

Verified with throwaway tests (GET query and POST form, repeated keys, single keys) and the full suite (`go test -count=1 ./...`) passes exactly as before, `go vet` clean.

Reproduced and understood: a second `e.Group("/group", ...)` overwrites the middleware bookkeeping for that prefix, so the first group's routes lose their handler/middleware chain and fall through to 404. I'm fixing the group registration so each group keeps its own middleware and both routes work. ETA ~10 min.

Diagnosed: in the gzip middleware's cleanup, when the handler writes an empty body `res.Size` stays 0, so the middleware strips `Content-Encoding` and discards the stream — but the gzip writer has already flushed its 10-byte header into the response, leaving orphan gzip bytes with no encoding header. I'm changing it so an empty body still produces a complete, valid gzip stream that keeps `Content-Encoding: gzip` (and `text/plain; charset=UTF-8`), while the 204/error paths stay as they are. ETA ~6 min.

Fixed in `middleware/compress.go`. The gzip writer flushes its 10-byte header on the first `Write` even for an empty slice, but `res.Size` stays 0, so the cleanup path deleted `Content-Encoding` and discarded the rest of the stream — leaving orphan gzip bytes with no encoding header.

Now the "nothing was written" cleanup only runs when the gzip writer was never used. For an empty 200 response the stream is closed normally, so you get a complete, valid gzip stream with `Content-Encoding: gzip` and `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8`; gunzipping yields an empty body. The 204 No Content and error-returned paths are unchanged, and all pre-existing gzip tests still pass.
